proposition: In the second subsection Nafsat I assembles Companion sayings (seven aḥruf with ẓāhir, bāṭin, ḥadd and maṭlaʿ; two kinds of knowledge; Abū Bakr's secret knowledge; ʿAlī's seventy camel loads; Ḥusayn on KHYʿṢ) to conclude that true knowledge is hidden from most people.

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, writing to the ruler who was judging him
Melvin-Koushki, The Quest for a Universal Science (Yale 2012)
